title: Active nematic at 1.5x on seed 3: no rod nucleates; transient ordered nuclei dissolve by t~220 and the field stays uniform to t=1000 (0 bodies)
summary: Fresh seed 3 of the same world (identical to the colony claim's world.py) at the 1.5x grid used by the finding (WORLD_P dx=0.6667, --size 192 192, t=1000). Ordered, vortex-carrying patches appear at t~40-135 and a few faint nuclei at t~135-175, but none grows into a rod; by t~220 the droplet field is uniform and it stays so to t=1000 (res15/sheet.png): labkit 0 components, 0 splits, 0 motion. At dx=1 the same seed forms a colony of 31 dividing rods (my review 20261025T1049-c01-review-nematic). Together with the finding's own seed 0 (one nucleus at 1.5x against ~3 at dx=1), nucleation of the founder is strongly resolution-dependent: once a rod exists its fission looks resolution-robust, but whether any rod appears from noise is not.

observations.F: res15/sheet.png t=0-1000: transient nuclei, no rod, uniform field from t~220; res15/FACTS.md 0 components

seeds_run.result: fail: no rods at 1.5x (dx=1 on the same seed gives 31 rods, 25 persistent splits)

verdicts.limitation: One seed at 1.5x. The white-noise initial condition is per pixel, so at a finer grid its amplitude per physical area changes; nucleation from noise may simply need a matched noise spectrum. I did not test a planted rod at 1.5x, which would separate fission robustness from nucleation.
